mainTopic: Blemishes of the legs and fingers that disqualify a כהן, the טומאה of an extra finger, and the count of a body's limbs and bones
overview: This amud joins the משנה partway through its list of מומין that disqualify a כהן: leg and foot deformities, joined or extra fingers, an extra digit on every limb, and a כהן who uses both hands equally. The גמרא learns from the extra word ״אוֹ״ in ״אוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל״ and ״אוֹ שֶׁבֶר יָד״ that other leg and hand blemishes count too. It also corrects a ברייתא so that it matches the משנה's ruling that fingers which were cut apart are fit. רבי יוחנן limits the rule of a cut-off extra finger to one that sits in line with the other fingers. The גמרא then turns to the טומאה of such an extra finger from a מת. A finger in the row is a full אבר. A finger out of the row is טמא only by touch and carrying, explained either as an עצם כשעורה or as a rabbinic גזירה with a deliberate sign of difference. Next comes the משנה in אהלות about most of a body's frame or most of its bones, where 125 bones is a fixed measure for every body. The amud ends with the 248 limbs of a man and the four extra limbs of a woman (hinges and doors, and according to רבי עקיבא a key). רב rules that these extra limbs do not spread טומאת אהל, and the גמרא shows that a man's צירים are only flesh.

steps.title: Leg and foot deformities that disqualify a priest
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of leg blemishes: בעל הפיקים, the עיקל (bowlegged), a protrusion by the thumb or big toe, a heel sticking out backward, and feet wide like a goose's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also disqualified: a בעל הפיקים and an עיקל. What is an עיקל? Anyone who puts his feet together, yet his knees do not touch each other. Also disqualified: one with a bump sticking out by his thumb or big toe, one whose heel sticks out backward, and one whose feet are wide like a goose's.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of listing body defects that make a כהן unfit to serve in the בית המקדש. Here it lists defects of the legs and feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list began earlier in the משנה, so we are joining it partway through. The משנה stops to define the unusual word עיקל. It is someone whose feet touch while his knees stay apart, which is what we call bowlegged. The other items describe parts of the foot that stick out or are shaped abnormally.

keyTerms.meaning: One with large bumps or knobs on his legs (defined later in the גמרא)
Bowlegged: feet touch but knees do not

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the עיקל is the opposite of the קישן (mentioned in the גמרא below), whose ankles knock together. Both count as leg blemishes.

phrases.english: and one with leg-knobs, and the ikkel.
phrases.notes: Continuing a list begun earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the ikkel?
phrases.notes: The משנה defines its own term.

phrases.english: Anyone who brings his feet together
and his knees do not knock against each other.
phrases.notes: In other words, bowlegged.

phrases.english: one with a bump sticking out from his thumb or big toe,
one whose heel sticks out backward,
one whose feet are wide like a goose's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of מומין from the previous amud (44b).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowlegged (עיקל), a bump protruding by the thumb or big toe, backward-protruding heel, and goose-like wide feet are all disqualifying blemishes.

steps.title: Joined fingers and a cut-off extra finger
steps.stepSummary: Fingers or toes stacked on each other, or joined together, disqualify a כהן. Joining only up to the joint is fine. Joining past the joint is fine once it has been cut apart. A cut-off extra finger disqualifies only if it had a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his fingers lie on top of one another, or are stuck together, he is unfit. If they are joined only from the top (the palm side) up to the middle joint, he is fit. If they are joined past the joint and he cut them apart, he is fit. If he had an extra finger and cut it off: if it had a bone in it, he is unfit; if not, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from legs to fingers and toes. It gives rules for joined fingers and for an extra finger that was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates a normal-looking minor joining (up to the joint) from a real defect. A defect that is fully fixed by cutting the fingers apart no longer disqualifies. An extra finger that contained a bone still disqualifies even after removal, because, as Rashi explains, once it is cut off he is missing a limb that was part of him.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying one on top of another

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'לְמַעְלָה' (above) means closer to the palm or sole, and 'לְמַטָּה' (below) means farther out toward the fingertip. This is the reverse of what a beginner might expect.

phrases.english: One whose fingers lie one on top of another,
or are joined together, [is unfit];
if joined from above until the joint, he is fit;
if joined below the joint and he cut it apart, he is fit;
if there was an extra finger on it and he cut it off,
if it has a bone, he is unfit,
and if not, he is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from leg and foot blemishes to finger and toe blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stacked or joined fingers disqualify. Joining up to the joint, or joining past the joint that was cut apart, is fit. A cut-off extra digit disqualifies only if it had a bone.

steps.title: An extra digit on every hand and foot
steps.stepSummary: A כהן with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot (24 in total): רבי יהודה says he is fit, and חכמים say he is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has an extra finger or toe on his hands and feet, six on each, making twenty-four in total, רבי יהודה declares him fit and חכמים declare him unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about a כהן who has an extra digit on all four limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is specifically symmetrical, six on each limb, the way the פסוק describes the giant in שמואל ב כא:כ. The גמרא on the next amud (45b) explains that both sides learn their view from that פסוק: רבי יהודה reads it as praise of the giant, so this is not a blemish, and חכמים read it as describing a defect.

keyTerms.meaning: Six and six (on each hand and foot)

phrases.english: One with extra [digits] on his hands and feet,
six and six, twenty-four in total,
Rabbi Yehuda declares him fit
and the Sages declare him unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the extra-finger topic to the case of an extra digit on every limb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי יהודה says fit, חכמים say unfit.

steps.title: A priest who uses both hands equally
steps.stepSummary: An ambidextrous כהן: רבי disqualifies him and חכמים declare him fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has full use of both hands: רבי declares him unfit, and חכמים declare him fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with another מחלוקת, about a כהן who is ambidextrous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is whether being equally skilled with both hands counts as a defect. רבי treats it as a blemish, and חכמים do not. The גמרא on the next amud (45b) gives the reason: רבי holds that he trained his left hand because his right hand had grown weak, while חכמים hold that his left hand gained strength and his right hand is still strong.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'רבי' here with 'רבי יהודה' in the line before. Plain 'רבי' always means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: One who controls both of his hands:
Rabbi declares him unfit
and the Sages declare him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the משנה, still about hands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי says unfit, חכמים say fit.

steps.title: Where do other leg defects come from in the verse?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the words 'שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל' only teach a broken leg, and asks for a source for the קישן, עיקל, and קילבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'A broken leg.' From this I only know about a broken leg. From where do I include the קישן, the עיקל, and the קילבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that asks for the תורה source behind the leg blemishes in the משנה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse explicitly mentions only a broken leg. The ברייתא asks how other leg deformities, which are not breaks at all, can also count as disqualifying blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: One whose knees or ankles knock together
One with a knob sticking out from his big toe (Rashi)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
'A broken leg'
I have only a broken leg,
from where do I include
the kishan, the ikkel, and the kilban?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶר רֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by seeking the scriptural source for the משנה's leg blemishes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse-based source showing that leg deformities other than a break also disqualify.

steps.title: The word 'or' includes other leg defects
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'אוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל'. The extra word 'אוֹ' includes all similar leg blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Or a broken leg.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question: the extra word 'אוֹ' (or) broadens the category beyond a simple break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said 'שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל'. The added 'אוֹ' is read as a רבוי (inclusion), bringing in the קישן, עיקל, and קילבן as leg blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or': here read as an extra word that includes more cases

steps.whatToRemember: Leg blemishes beyond an actual break are learned from the extra word 'אוֹ' in ״אוֹ שֶׁבֶר רָגֶל״.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'Or a broken leg.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'אוֹ' in the verse includes other leg deformities.

steps.title: Another teaching adds two more leg blemishes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בעל הקיפין and a שופנר are also blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: one with leg-knobs (בעל הקיפין) and the שופנר [are blemished].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a short ברייתא that lists two more leg blemishes. This sets up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names the terms without explaining them. בעל הקיפין is the same as the משנה's בעל הפיקים. The שופנר is a new term.

keyTerms.meaning: One whose leg has no knobs at all

steps.confusionAlert: 'קיפין' and 'פיקין' are the same word with the letters swapped. They are not two different blemishes.

phrases.english: It was taught: one with leg-knobs and the shufnar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further ברייתא about leg blemishes, tying back to בעל הפיקים in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעל הקיפין and שופנר are blemishes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן defines the two opposite terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains: a בעל הפיקין has many large protrusions on his leg, and a שופנר has none at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A בעל הפיקין is one who has many protrusions. A שופנר is one who has no protrusions at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defines the two terms from the ברייתא, showing they are opposite extremes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both too much and too little count as a defect. Excessive knobs on the leg are a blemish (Rashi: his ankle bone is very large), and a leg completely missing the normal knobs is also a blemish. This also explains the term בעל הפיקים from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Protrusions or knobs (literally 'cushions') on the leg

steps.whatToRemember: בעל הפיקין has too many leg knobs and שופנר has none. Both extremes are blemishes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A ba'al hapikin is
one who has many protrusions;
a shufnar is
one who has no protrusions at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּעַל הַפִּיקִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms listed in the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעל הפיקין has many leg protrusions; a שופנר has none at all.

steps.title: משנה quote: bump by the thumb and a heel sticking out back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two blemishes from the משנה: a bump growing out by the thumb or big toe, and a heel that sticks out backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has a bump coming out of his thumb, or whose heel sticks out behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both blemishes are a strange shape of the hand or foot. The 'heel sticking out' sounds unclear, so the גמרא will explain what it really means.

keyTerms.meaning: A bump or knob growing out

phrases.english: A bump coming out of his thumb,
phrases.notes: This applies to the thumb or the big toe.

phrases.english: and his heel sticks out behind him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the leg blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bump by the thumb and a heel that sticks out backward are blemishes.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains the heel that sticks out
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says it means the lower leg comes down into the middle of the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: His lower leg comes out in the middle of his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains what the משנה means by 'his heel sticks out behind him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the leg meets the foot near the back, over the heel. Here the leg meets the foot in the middle, so a large part of the foot sticks out behind the leg. That is what looks like a protruding heel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
His lower leg comes out in the middle of his foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second blemish quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Heel sticks out' means the leg is attached to the middle of the foot.

steps.title: משנה quote: feet wide like a goose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's blemish of feet that are wide like a goose's.
steps.simpleTranslation: His feet are wide like those of a goose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goose has flat, wide feet with webbing between the toes. So it is unclear which feature makes this a blemish: the flatness, or the joined toes.

phrases.english: His feet are wide like those of a goose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Goose-like wide feet are a blemish.

steps.title: רב פפא: flat feet alone are enough
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the blemish is flat feet, even if the toes are separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Do not say the blemish is only when the feet are flat and the toes are not split. Rather, once the feet are flat, it is a blemish even if the toes are split.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains which part of 'like a goose' counts. Flatness alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the foot must be exactly like a goose's, both flat and with joined toes. רב פפא says no. The flatness by itself makes him blemished, even if his toes are normal and separate.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the toes must be joined like a goose's. According to רב פפא, flat feet alone are a blemish.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say it means flat and not split,
rather, once it is flat,
it is a blemish even though the toes are split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the goose comparison in step 11 goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flat feet are a blemish even if the toes are split.

steps.title: משנה quote: fingers on top of each other or joined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's blemish of fingers that lie on top of one another or are joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: His fingers lie one on top of the other, or are joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a ברייתא that finds a source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה adds a detail: if the joined fingers are separated by cutting, the כהן is fit. That detail is important for the question the גמרא will ask in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying on top of one another (overlapping)

phrases.aramaic: אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו מוּרְכָּבוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: His fingers lie one on top of the other,
or are joined together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו מוּרְכָּבוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overlapping or joined fingers are a blemish. If they were cut apart, the כהן is fit.

steps.title: ברייתא: what is the source for joined fingers?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'שבר יד' teaches only a broken hand, and asks for a source for overlapping or joined fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'A broken hand' teaches me only a broken hand. Where do we learn fingers that overlap above, or are joined above the joint (and he cut them apart)?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא asks where the פסוק teaches the finger blemishes, since the words 'שבר יד' only mention a broken hand. This is just like the leg question earlier (step 5).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's question, as first worded, refers to fingers that were joined and then cut apart. That wording leads straight to the problem the גמרא raises in the next step.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁבֶר יָד״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶר יָד.
phrases.english: 'A broken hand': I have only a broken hand.
Fingers overlapping above,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's original wording implies 'and he cut them, from where do we know?'

phrases.english: or joined above the joint, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן שֶׁבֶר יָד אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶר יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a פסוק source for the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the פסוק for the finger blemishes, since 'שבר יד' mentions only a broken hand.

steps.title: But the משנה said that case is fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks into the ברייתא: the משנה said that if the fingers were cut apart, the כהן is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said he is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops in the middle of the ברייתא to point out a contradiction with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls fingers that were joined and then cut apart a blemish. But the משנה clearly says such a כהן is fit. The two cannot both be right as worded. (Rashi: the ברייתא's 'above the joint' is the משנה's 'below the joint', the part toward the nail; they simply count from opposite ends of the finger.)

phrases.english: But you said he is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording, which treats fingers that were cut apart as a blemish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that once the joined fingers are cut apart he is fit, so the ברייתא cannot call that case a blemish.

steps.title: Correcting the ברייתא: he did not cut them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא's wording: it is talking about fingers that were not cut apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it: 'and he did not cut them' — from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it matches the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is really about fingers still joined above the joint, which were never cut. Those are a blemish. Fingers that were cut apart remain fit, just as the משנה says.

phrases.english: Rather: and he did not cut them — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction (changing the case in the ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls fingers that were cut apart a blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about joined fingers that were not cut, which matches the משנה.

steps.title: The source: 'אוֹ שבר יד'
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'אוֹ' in 'או שבר יד' includes the finger blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Or a broken hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question: the extra word 'אוֹ' includes joined and overlapping fingers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works exactly like 'או שבר רגל' for the legs (step 6). The word 'אוֹ' widens the blemish from a broken hand to other similar hand blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: Or (an extra word used to include more cases)

steps.whatToRemember: 'או שבר יד' includes finger blemishes, but only fingers still joined. Fingers that were cut apart are fit.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'Or a broken hand.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the corrected question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'אוֹ' in 'או שבר יד' includes joined or overlapping fingers that were not cut.

steps.title: משנה quote: an extra finger that was cut off
steps.stepSummary: If an extra finger was cut off, he is disqualified if it had a bone, and fit if it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had an extra finger and cut it off: if it has a bone, he is disqualified; if not, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה. This sets up רבי יוחנן's limit in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra finger with a bone counts as a real limb. Cutting it off makes him like someone missing a limb, so he stays disqualified. Without a bone, it was just extra flesh, so removing it leaves him fit.

phrases.english: If he had an extra finger and cut it off,
if it has a bone, he is disqualified,
and if not, he is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut-off extra finger with a bone disqualifies; one without a bone does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only if it sits in line with the other fingers
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only when the extra finger is in the row of fingers along the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This applies only when it is counted along the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's rule about a cut-off extra finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra finger counts as a real limb only if it sits in line with the other fingers. Only then does a bone in it make him disqualified after it is cut off. An extra growth somewhere else on the hand is not treated as a real finger.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: A cut-off extra finger disqualifies only if it had a bone AND sat in line with the other fingers.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
And this is only when it is counted along the back of the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְהוּא שֶׁנִּסְפֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule about a cut-off extra finger with a bone applies only when it sits in line with the other fingers.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the טומאה of an extra finger with a bone
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an extra finger with a bone but no nail makes things טמא by touch, by carrying, and in an אהל (Rashi: when a little flesh is still on it), and that it counts toward the 125 bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: An extra finger that has a bone but no nail makes things impure by touching and by carrying, and also makes things impure in a tent. It also counts toward the number of 125 bones. [Rashi: this case has a little flesh still on it.]
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the טומאה of an extra finger cut from a dead body. It moves from the topic of מומים to a related question about טומאת מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rashi explains the case: a little flesh (less than a כזית) is still on it, and it lines up with the other fingers. So it is treated like a full אבר מן המת, even without a nail, and an אבר gives all three kinds of טומאה, including טומאת אהל, even with less than a כזית of flesh. With no flesh at all, it would not give טומאת אהל by itself, but it counts as one of the 125 bones that make up the majority of a body's bones (רוב מנין).

keyTerms.meaning: Touching and carrying, two ways of becoming טמא
Impurity spread to everything under the same roof as a corpse or corpse part
125, the majority of the 248 bones in the body

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An extra finger that has a bone in it,
but has no nail —
makes things impure by touching and by carrying,
and makes things impure in a tent,
and it counts toward the number of 125 bones.
phrases.notes: 125 is the majority of the 248 bones. A majority of bones makes things טמא in an אהל even with no flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from extra fingers as a מום in a כהן to the related topic of their טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra finger with a bone, even without a nail, is a full אבר for all טומאה when a little flesh is on it (Rashi), and it counts toward the 125 bones.

steps.title: Only when the finger is in the row along the hand
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן limits the ברייתא to an extra finger that lines up with the other fingers on the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is only when it is counted along the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the ברייתא and explains which kind of extra finger it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's strong ruling (full אבר, טמא even in an אהל) applies only when the extra finger sits in the row with the other fingers. That makes it look like a real finger, so it counts as a true אבר. This matches the same rule we saw in step 19 about מומים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is counted, meaning it lines up in the row with the other fingers

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
And this is when it is counted along the back of the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's full-אבר ruling applies only to an extra finger in line with the other fingers.

steps.title: רב: touch and carrying, but not in an אהל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes his great teacher רב, who rules that an extra finger with a bone and no nail makes things טמא by touch and carrying but not in an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, may God be his help: An extra finger that has a bone but no nail makes things impure by touching and carrying, but does not make things impure in a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ruling from רב that seems to contradict the ברייתא, because רב says the finger does not make things טמא in an אהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case sounds exactly the same as the ברייתא: a bone and no nail. But the result is different. רב treats the finger only partly like an אבר: it gives טומאה by touch and carrying, but not in an אהל. This sets up the question of how the two rulings fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Our great teacher, here meaning רב
May God be his help, a blessing for a revered teacher
An extra finger (another spelling of יתירה)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This matter was said by our great teacher,
phrases.notes: Meaning רב.

phrases.english: may the Omnipresent be his help:
An extra finger that has a bone
but has no nail —
makes things impure by touching and by carrying,
but does not make things impure in a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דָּבָר זֶה רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּדוֹל אֲמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that seems to conflict with the ברייתא in step 20 about טומאת אהל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra finger with a bone and no nail makes things טמא by touch and carrying, but not in an אהל.

steps.title: רב's ruling is about a finger not in the row
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן explains that רב's ruling is about an extra finger that is not in line with the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And this is when it is not counted along the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits רב's ruling to a different case. This settles the clash with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two rulings do not argue. A finger in the row with the other fingers is a full אבר, so it gives all טומאה, as the ברייתא said. A finger out of the row gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל, as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not counted, meaning it is not in line with the other fingers

steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings talk about a finger with a bone and no nail. The only difference is where the finger sits on the hand: in the row (ברייתא) or out of the row (רב).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
And this is when it is not counted along the back of the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines רב's case so it no longer conflicts with the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's partial-טומאה ruling applies to an extra finger that is not in line with the other fingers.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: this ruling has no clear logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן complains that the ruling for a finger out of the row is like prophecy: either it is an אבר and should make things טמא in an אהל, or it is not and should not make things טמא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They made their words like words of prophecy, with no reason given. Whichever way you look at it: if it is a limb, it should also make things impure in a tent. And if it is not a limb, it should not make things impure even by touching and carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks the logic of the middle ruling for a finger that is not in the row. He uses a מה נפשך (either way) argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבר מן המת gives all three kinds of טומאה, including אהל. If this finger is an אבר, there is no reason to leave out אהל. If it is not an אבר, there is no reason it should give טומאה by touch and carrying. A half-way ruling seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Like words of prophecy, a ruling with no reason that can be explained
Whichever way you look at it, an either-way argument
A limb: bone with flesh, which gives full טומאת מת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They made their words like words of prophecy,
phrases.notes: Meaning a rule with no reason we can see.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
If it is a limb —
it should also make things impure in a tent,
and if it is not a limb —
it should not make things impure by touching and carrying either!

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשׂוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם כְּדִבְרֵי נְבִיאוּת, מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of רב's ruling as it was defined in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that an out-of-row extra finger gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An either-way argument: an אבר gives all טומאה, and a non-אבר gives none, so a half-way status makes no sense.

steps.title: It is treated as a bone the size of a barley grain
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח explains that the חכמים gave this finger the status of an עצם כשעורה, which gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא son of רב איקא: They treated it as a bone the size of a barley grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר מנוח, in the name of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, answers רבי יוחנן's question by giving the ruling a clear basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finger out of the row is not an אבר at all. Instead, the חכמים gave it the law of an עצם כשעורה, a bone piece the size of a barley grain. That kind of bone gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל, so the middle ruling fits exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone the size of a barley grain, which gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל
They touched on it, meaning they gave it a ruling or status

steps.whatToRemember: An extra finger with a bone: if it is in the row with the other fingers, it is a full אבר and gives all טומאה, even in an אהל. If it is out of the row, it has the law of an עצם כשעורה: touch and carrying only, not אהל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a status that seems 'in between' can really be an existing, known category (עצם כשעורה) and not a rule with no reason.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoach said

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: in the name of Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika:
Because of the rule of a bone the size of a barley grain
they gave it a ruling.
phrases.notes: They gave it the status of an עצם כשעורה, not of an אבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's either-way challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Puts the case into a known category (עצם כשעורה) instead of the אבר category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to treat the finger as half an אבר, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not an אבר at all. It has the law of an עצם כשעורה, which gives טומאה by touch and carrying but not in an אהל.

steps.title: רב פפא: a rabbinic decree because of the finger in line
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a second answer to רבי יוחנן's complaint. The out-of-line finger is טמא only because of a גזירה, so people do not confuse it with the in-line finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a decree. The finger that is not counted with the others is made טמא because of the finger that is counted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way to answer רבי יוחנן's question from step 24. He says the טומאה of the out-of-line finger is a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra finger that lines up with the hand is a real אבר and is טמא מדאורייתא. The חכמים worried that people would mix it up with an extra finger that is out of line. So they gave the out-of-line finger some טומאה as well. This answer is different from רב הונא בר מנוח's comparison to an עצם כשעורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים
Counted, meaning lined up in the row with the other fingers
Because of, on account of (a different case)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is a decree that the one that is not counted [is impure],
phrases.notes: The finger out of line with the hand

phrases.english: because of the one that is counted.
phrases.notes: The in-line finger, which is a real limb

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to רבי יוחנן's קשיא, offered alongside רב הונא בר מנוח's answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed illogical, because a finger should be either fully an אבר or not טמא at all
steps.terutzMaskana: מדאורייתא it is not an אבר. The חכמים made it partly טמא as a fence because of the in-line finger.

steps.title: Then it should also be טמא in an אהל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. If this is a decree because of the in-line finger, the decree should copy all of that finger's טומאה, including טומאת אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the finger that is not counted should also make things טמא in an אהל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer. If the חכמים were worried about confusion, they should have made the finger טמא in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The in-line finger is טמא by touch, by carrying, and באהל. A decree meant to prevent confusion would seem to need the same full set of rules. Stopping halfway seems to defeat the purpose.

phrases.english: If so,
the one that is not counted should also make things impure in a tent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's גזירה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that the טומאה is a rabbinic decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A decree made to prevent confusion should copy all of the original's rules, including טומאת אהל

steps.title: The חכמים left a sign so no תרומה is burned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים purposely left out טומאת אהל. That way people know this טומאה is only rabbinic and will not burn תרומה or קדשים because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים made a sign of difference. This is so that people will not burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The partial טומאה was left that way on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is טמא only מדרבנן may not be burned, because מדאורייתא it is still pure. If the out-of-line finger were טמא in every way, people would think it is a Torah-level טומאה. They might then burn holy food that is really pure. Leaving out אהל shows everyone that this is only a rabbinic טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A distinguishing sign, a recognizable difference
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The out-of-line extra finger is טמא by touch and carrying but not באהל. This difference shows that its טומאה is only rabbinic, so no one burns pure holy food because of it.

phrases.english: The Sages made a distinguishing sign,
so that people will not burn
teruma and consecrated items on account of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב פפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A decree should copy every rule of the original case
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים purposely left out טומאת אהל so people know the טומאה is rabbinic and do not burn pure תרומה or קדשים

steps.title: The משנה about most of a corpse's frame or bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in אהלות. Most of the frame or most of the number of bones of a מת is טמא, even if together they are less than a רובע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Most of the frame or most of the number of bones of a dead person is טמא, even if it is less than a quarter-קב of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from מסכת אהלות. This sets up the next discussion about counting bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, bones of a מת make things טמא באהל when they fill a רובע הקב. This משנה adds two other measures: most of the body's frame, or most of its number of bones. Either one is טמא even below that volume.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the body's frame or structure
Most of the body's number of bones
A quarter of a קב, the normal volume measure for bones of a מת

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב בִּנְיָנוֹ וְרוֹב מִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל מֵת,
phrases.english: The majority of the structure or the majority of the number [of bones] of a corpse,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוֹבַע —
phrases.english: even though there is not a quarter [kav] in it,
are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about counting bones
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most of the frame or most of the number of bones of a מת is טמא even below a רובע

steps.title: A ברייתא defines both majorities
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's terms. Most of the frame means two shins and one thigh. Most of the number means 125 bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is most of the frame? Two shins and one thigh, since they make up most of a full-sized person's height. What is most of the number? One hundred twenty-five bones.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא defines the two terms from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the frame is measured by height. Two shins and one thigh make up more than half of a full-sized person's height (Rashi: one who is not a dwarf; the head is not counted). Most of the number is measured by counting bones. 125 is a majority of the normal 248 bones.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What is the majority of the structure?
Two shins and one thigh,
since that is most of his height in a full-sized person.
What is the majority of the number?
One hundred and twenty-five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms used in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most of the frame is two shins and one thigh. Most of the number is 125 bones.

steps.title: Why teach simple arithmetic?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא why the ברייתא bothered to say 125. Everyone can work out that 125 is more than half of 248.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Did the תנא come to teach us arithmetic?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the ברייתא. Saying 125 seems pointless, since it is just the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. A ברייתא should teach a new הלכה, not a fact anyone can calculate. So what new idea is hidden in the number 125?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Did the tanna come to teach us a number?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the ברייתא needed to state 125
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement of the number 125
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 125 is obviously a majority of 248, so stating it seems to add nothing new

steps.title: 125 counts for every body
steps.stepSummary: The number 125 teaches that it is a fixed measure. It applies even to a body with only 200 bones or with 281 bones, because we follow most people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us what a ברייתא says: A body that is missing bones and has only 200, or has extra bones and has 281, all are measured by the count of 125. Go after the majority of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the number 125 is a fixed amount. It is not simply half of whatever bones this particular body has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the majority depends on each body's own count, so a body with 281 bones would need 141. The ברייתא says no: 125 always counts, because most people have 248 bones. This connects back to the extra finger, since extra bones do not change the measure.
steps.whatToRemember: רוב מנינו is always 125 bones. This is true whether a body has fewer or more bones than normal, because the measure follows the majority of people (248 bones).
steps.confusionAlert: 125 is not 'half plus one' of this specific body. For a body with 200 bones, 125 is more than half. For a body with 281 bones, 125 is less than half. It still counts in both cases.

phrases.english: It teaches us as it was taught [in a baraita]:
Lacking, that has only two hundred,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵר, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מָאתַיִם וּשְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד —
phrases.english: and extra, that has two hundred eighty-one,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן עוֹלִין לְמִנְיַן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: all of them count toward the number of one hundred twenty-five,
go after the majority of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals a hidden חידוש in the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number 125 seemed to be just simple arithmetic
steps.terutzMaskana: 125 is a fixed measure for every body, based on the majority of people

steps.title: The students of רבי ישמעאל count 252 limbs
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells a story: the students of רבי ישמעאל boiled the body of an executed woman and counted 252 limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There was a story with the students of רבי ישמעאל. They boiled the body of a זונה whom the king had sentenced to burning. They checked and found 252 limbs in her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life story about counting the limbs of a human body. The count came out to 252, not the expected 248, and this sets up a puzzle that the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא worked with the standard count of 248 limbs. Here an actual count gives 252, which is four too many. The boiling was done to separate the flesh from the bones so the bones could be counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident that really happened
They boiled (to remove the flesh from the bones)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה, the main student of שמואל.

phrases.english: There was an incident with the students of Rabbi Yishmael
who boiled the body of a certain prostitute
who had been sentenced by the king to burning,
they examined and found in her
252 limbs,
phrases.notes: Four more than the usual 248.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִידָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the fixed count of 248 and 125 to a real count that came out different.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An actual count of a woman's body found 252 limbs.

steps.title: A woman has four extra limbs
steps.stepSummary: The 252 is explained: they counted a woman, and the פסוק gives a woman two extra 'hinges' and two extra 'doors'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Maybe you examined a woman? The פסוק added to her two hinges and two doors.
steps.whatsHappening: The puzzle of 252 is answered. The body was a woman's, and a woman has four limbs that a man does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 248 count is for a man. A woman has four more, two 'hinges' and two 'doors', which adds up to 252. The next steps show which פסוקים teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: Hinges (here, body parts that work like a door's hinges)

steps.confusionAlert: The 248 limbs in the famous count are a man's. This does not contradict the count, because a woman simply has four extra.

phrases.english: He said to them: Perhaps you examined a woman,
for the verse added to her
two hinges and two doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzle raised by the count of 252.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the body was a woman's, not a man's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of 248 seemed to be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: 248 is a man's count. A woman has four extra limbs, so 252.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a woman has hinges
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אלעזר learns from a פסוק that just as a house has hinges, a woman has hinges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר says: Just as a house has hinges, a woman has hinges. As it says: 'And she knelt and gave birth, for her pains (צִרֶיהָ) turned upon her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows where the 'hinges' come from. רבי אלעזר reads the word צִרֶיהָ as 'her hinges'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צִרֶיהָ normally means 'her pains', but it sounds like צִירִים, hinges. In childbirth these 'hinges' turn, the way a door swings on its hinges. This gives a source for the extra limbs mentioned in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: Her pains, read here as 'her hinges'

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Elazar says:
Just as a house has hinges —
so too a woman has hinges,
as it is stated: 'And she knelt and gave birth,
phrases.notes: שמואל א ד:יט

phrases.english: for her pains (hinges) turned upon her.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁצִּירִים לַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the 'hinges' mentioned in the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman has hinges, learned from צִרֶיהָ.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a woman has doors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע learns from a פסוק in איוב that just as a house has doors, a woman has doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Just as a house has doors, a woman has doors. As it says: 'For it did not shut the doors of my womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second תנא. רבי יהושע gives the source for the 'doors'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks openly of 'the doors of my womb', which shows that a woman has 'doors'. Together with רבי אלעזר's hinges, this gives the two pairs that explain the four extra limbs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Just as a house has doors —
so too a woman has doors,
as it is stated: 'For it did not shut the doors of my womb.'
phrases.notes: איוב ג:י

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁדְּלָתוֹת לַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second תנא in the same ברייתא, giving the source for 'doors'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman has doors, learned from דַּלְתֵי בִטְנִי.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a woman has a key
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds that just as a house has a key, a woman has a key, learned from 'and He opened her womb'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Just as a house has a key, a woman has a key. As it says: 'And He opened her womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי עקיבא, who adds a third 'house part', a key. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening needs a key, so רבי עקיבא learns from וַיִּפְתַּח that a woman has a 'key'. That is one more limb, which would make the total 253, not 252.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Just as a house has a key,
so too a woman has a key,
as it is stated: 'And He opened her womb.'
phrases.notes: בראשית ל:כב

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ לַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth extra limb beyond the hinges and doors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman also has a key, so five extra limbs in all.

steps.title: The story challenges רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The story of רבי ישמעאל's students found only four extra limbs, which seems to go against רבי עקיבא's fifth one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story of רבי ישמעאל's students is a difficulty for רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא from the story at the start. They found 252, only four extra, with no 'key'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman has hinges, doors, and a key, that is five extra limbs, so the count should have been 253. The real count found only 252. The story seems to show that the key does not exist.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Akiva, it is difficult —
from the students of Rabbi Yishmael!
phrases.notes: They counted only 252, not 253.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קַשְׁיָא דְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי עקיבא's view against the count in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that a woman has a key
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An actual count found 252, four extra, with no room for a fifth limb.

steps.title: The tiny key dissolved in the boiling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'key' is very small, so it may have dissolved when the body was boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, since it is small, it dissolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי עקיבא. The key may have been there and dissolved during the boiling, so the students did not find it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only shows what was left after the boiling, not what was there before. A tiny limb could melt away. So the count of 252 does not disprove רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Perhaps, since it is small,
it dissolved completely (in the boiling).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weakening the proof: the evidence is not complete.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of 252 shows there is no key.
steps.terutzMaskana: The key may have existed and dissolved, so the story does not disprove רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman has four extra limbs (hinges and doors), and according to רבי עקיבא a fifth, the key, which is tiny and can dissolve.

steps.title: רב: the extra limbs do not carry tent impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a woman's extra limbs do not spread טומאת אהל, because that law covers only what is the same in all people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: And all of them do not make things טמא in an אהל. As it says: 'This is the law: a person (אדם) who dies in a tent.' This teaches a thing that is the same for every person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a הלכה about these extra limbs. A woman's extra limbs do not spread טומאה under a roof the way a regular limb of a מת does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of טומאת אהל uses the word אָדָם, a person in general. רב reads this to mean only limbs that every person has, male or female. Limbs found only in women are therefore left out of טומאת אהל.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them (all the extra limbs)
Make things טמא by being under the same roof
Something that is the same for all people

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the discussion back to טומאת מת. The count of limbs matters for הלכה, and here the extra limbs are an exception for טומאת אהל, even though they are real limbs.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying these are not real limbs. They are limbs, but they are an exception for the specific law of טומאת אהל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: וְכוּלָּן אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל,
phrases.english: Rav said: And all of them do not impart impurity in a tent,
as it is stated: 'This is the law:
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:יד

phrases.english: when a person dies in a tent' —
meaning, something that is equal for all people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: וְכוּלָּן אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying the extra limbs to their halachic status for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Limbs found only in a woman do not spread טומאת אהל, because the פסוק says אָדָם, meaning what all people share.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טומאת אהל applies only to limbs that every human being has.

steps.title: אביי asks: don't men also have hinges?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the claim that צירים are unique to a woman, using a פסוק in ישעיה where a man (the prophet) speaks of his own צירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do men really not have hinges? But it is written: 'Pangs (tzirim) have taken hold of me, like the pangs of a woman giving birth'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the earlier idea that only a woman has צירים among her extra limbs. He points to ישעיה, a man, who says he has צירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching listed צירים as one of a woman's extra limbs, which implies a man has none. אביי reads the word צירים in the פסוק as 'hinges.' Since the prophet speaks about his own body, it seems a man has צירים too.

keyTerms.meaning: Hinges. Here it refers to hinge-like parts of the body. The same word can also mean pains or pangs.
And in a man there are none?

steps.confusionAlert: The word צִירִים has two meanings: 'pangs/pains' and 'hinges.' אביי's challenge depends on reading the פסוק as speaking about the body's hinges.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And in a man there are none?
But isn't it written:
"Pangs have taken hold of me, like the pangs of a woman giving birth"!
phrases.notes: ישעיה כא:ג. The speaker is a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that a woman's צירים are extra limbs that a man lacks.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that צירים are unique to a woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man (ישעיה) speaks of having צירים, so men must have them too.

steps.title: Answer: a man's hinges are only flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the צירים a man has are made only of flesh, with no bone, so they are not counted as limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are hinges of flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier teaching. A man does have צירים, but only fleshy ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a part that contains bone counts as a true limb (אבר). A man's צירים have no bone, so they do not count. A woman's צירים do contain bone, which is why they count as her extra limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: Hinges made of flesh only, with no bone
A limb. To count as one, it must contain bone.

phrases.english: Those are hinges of flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: these are a different kind of צירים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A man has צירים just like a woman, so they are not her extra limbs.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man's צירים are only flesh, not bony limbs, so the woman's bony צירים are still extra.

steps.title: A second verse: Daniel's hinges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another פסוק, from דניאל, where a man speaks of his own צירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'My lord, because of the vision my hinges (tzirai) have turned over'!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues with a second proof that men have צירים. This time the speaker is דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דניאל says his own צירים 'turned over.' That sounds like real body parts that can move or shift. This seems to show that men have true hinges.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"My lord, because of the vision my hinges have turned over"!
phrases.notes: דניאל י:טז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that men lack bony צירים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דניאל, a man, describes his own צירים turning over.

steps.title: Same answer: these are also hinges of flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: דניאל's צירים were also only flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, those are hinges of flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier answer. The צירים in דניאל are also fleshy and not bony limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is needed to answer this second פסוק. The same distinction between fleshy hinges and bony hinges handles it.

phrases.english: Here too, those are hinges of flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from דניאל the same way as step 42.

steps.title: Proof from the count of 248 limbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer: if men had bony hinges, the famous count of 248 limbs would not work for a man or for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense this way. For if you do not say so, how could you find 248 limbs? Neither in a man nor in a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the answer it just gave. The well-known number of 248 limbs only works if a man's hinges are flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man has exactly 248 limbs, and a woman has those plus four extra. If a man also had bony hinges, his count would be more than 248. A woman would then not have 248 either, since she has extra limbs. So the number 248 would not fit anyone, which shows that a man's hinges must be only flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (introduces supporting logic)
For if you do not say so
248, the number of limbs in a person

steps.whatToRemember: A man's צירים are only flesh and do not count as limbs. Only a woman's bony צירים are extra limbs. This keeps the count of 248 limbs for a man correct.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if you do not say so,
the 248 limbs
how could you find them?
Neither in a man nor in a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives logical support to the answers in steps 42 and 44.
steps.raayaObject: That a man's צירים are only flesh
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted count of 248 limbs, which must fit exactly for a man
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Men have only fleshy צירים, and a woman's bony צירים are her extra limbs.
